rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance: annual CPI-based rent increase cap (max 4%)
rules.requirement: When a lease expires, or a periodic tenant's lease ends, a landlord may not request or receive a rent increase above the percentage change in the CPI-U for the New York-northern New Jersey-Long Island area. The change is measured from the CPI 15 months before the month of the increase to the CPI 3 months before it. The increase may never exceed 4%. Rent may not rise by more than these percentages in any consecutive 12-month period, regardless of new tenants, a change of owner or a vacancy. The annual increase is not allowed if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance with housing codes, or if the landlord has not registered under § 19:2-9.8. The landlord must give the tenant and the Rent Regulation Officer written notice at least 30 days ahead. The notice must state the proposed increase and percentage, the prior year's rent, and the allowable increase amount and percentage. Tax, major new improvement and utility surcharges and hardship increases go through separate Board processes. The Board may not grant increases totaling more than 25% for any tenant in one year (§ 19:2-22). Rent collected above the legal amount must be rebated, retroactive up to two years. Violations carry fines of $100 to $2,000 or up to 90 days' imprisonment per housing space, and the Board may impose penalties up to $500.
rules.key_value: Annual increase capped at the CPI-U change (from 15 months before to 3 months before the increase month), never above 4%; one increase per 12 months; 30 days' written notice to tenant and Rent Regulation Officer; Board-granted increases capped at 25% a year in total

new_construction_exemption.basis: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from limits on periodic increases for the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years after completion of construction (issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy), whichever is shorter. The exemption is 30 years if there is no initial mortgage financing. The landlord must apply to the Rent Control Board for certification.

unverifiable_exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings certified as exempt by the Rent Control Board (up to 30 years)
Vacant dwellings exempt for 5 years after a Board-determined substantial rehabilitation
Units rehabilitated under federal or state Rental Rehabilitation Programs that receive Section 8 subsidies or federal vouchers
Units under a landlord contract with a governmental agency that regulates the rent
coverage.summary: All multiple dwellings (any building with one or more apartments rented or offered for rent) are subject to rent control. Exempt: public housing, hotel or motel space rented day to day to transients, commercial space, newly constructed multiple dwellings (up to 30 years), substantially rehabilitated vacant dwellings (5 years), certain Section 8 rehabilitation units, and units under a governmental agency rent-regulation contract.
coverage.owner_conditions: The chapter defines 'owner occupied' (four units or fewer, with the owner living in one), but does not list owner-occupied dwellings as exempt. The definition is used only for the inspection-fee waiver.
coverage.other_conditions: The landlord must register annually and the dwelling must be in substantial compliance before any annual increase.

rules.exemptions: Public housing; hotel or motel space rented day to day to transients; space rented for commercial use; newly constructed multiple dwellings (initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years from the Certificate of Occupancy, whichever is shorter, on application to the Rent Control Board); vacant dwellings substantially rehabilitated (5 years); units rehabilitated under Rental Rehabilitation Programs that receive Section 8 subsidies or vouchers; units under a governmental agency rent-regulation contract.
rules.effective_date_note: Under § 19:2-21, rents were first controlled when the chapter was adopted on September 4, 1985, and the chapter continues in force from October 19, 1988. The current section text comes from Ord. 6 PSF-A(S) (9-5-2017) as amended by Ord. 6PSF-I (9-18-2024). The text does not say when the 4% ceiling began.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.review_note: § 19:2-7.1 refers to registration at 'subsection 19:1-10', which looks like a mistaken reference to § 19:2-9.8. Ord. No. 6PSF-I is cited for both the 8-2-2023 and the 9-18-2024 amendments. The State has no general rent cap, so no state rule applies on precedence.
rules.source_notes: Official Newark code text (DX21). The 'Saturday, October 3, 2026' header is the date the code was printed, not an enactment date.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance: retaliatory eviction bar
rules.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under the rent control chapter. The chapter's statement of policy mentions the fear of eviction without just cause. However, the chapter itself lists no allowed eviction causes, notice periods or relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: No eviction action as reprisal for a tenant's efforts to secure or enforce rights under the rent control chapter

coverage.summary: Applies to dwelling units covered by the Newark rent control chapter: all multiple dwellings except the exempt dwellings listed in § 19:2-2.

rules.exemptions: Dwellings exempt from the rent control chapter (see § 19:2-2).
rules.effective_date_note: Section adopted by Ord. 6 PSF-A(S) on 9-5-2017 and amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I. The chapter itself dates from 1985. No separate effective date is stated for this section.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.
rules.review_note: This is reprisal protection only; the chapter has no general just-cause list. Statewide good-cause and reprisal protections come from the Anti-Eviction Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1) and N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10, which are recorded at state level.

rules.title: Newark protected tenancy applications for senior and disabled tenants facing condominium or cooperative conversion
rules.requirement: The Administrator of the Office of Rent Control accepts applications from senior citizen tenants and disabled tenants to decide whether they qualify for protected tenancy against eviction caused by a condominium or cooperative conversion. The Administrator may appoint a Hearing Officer. Decisions follow the eligibility standards of the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22). The landlord pays a $350 fee when a Hearing Officer is appointed, plus $30 for each tenant the Board must notify. The Rent Control Board hears appeals from the Administrator's or Hearing Officer's decisions.
rules.key_value: Local application process for protected tenancy on condo/co-op conversion; landlord pays $350 Hearing Officer fee and $30 per tenant notified

unverifiable_exemptions: Tenant eligibility as a senior citizen or disabled tenant under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22 et seq.
coverage.summary: Senior citizen and disabled tenants in Newark buildings undergoing condominium or cooperative conversion.
coverage.other_conditions: Triggered only by a condominium or cooperative conversion. Eligibility follows the state protected tenancy standards.

rules.effective_date_note: Section adopted by Ord. 6 PSF-A(S) on 9-5-2017 and amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I. No separate effective date is stated.
rules.quoted_span: The Administrator of the Office of Rent Control shall be empowered to accept applications from senior citizen tenants or disabled tenants for the purpose of determining their eligibility for protected tenancy status from eviction resulting from condominium or cooperative conversions.
rules.review_note: This is the local process that carries out the state Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act. The substantive protection comes from N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22 et seq., which is recorded at state level.
